hero.tagline: Full-stack Go web framework with React pages.
hero.sub: The whole app compiles into one executable. It runs on a 1 CPU / 1 GB VPS with no Node, no Redis and no reverse proxy, and `tifa deploy` puts it live.
hero.description: The whole app compiles into one executable. It runs on a 1 CPU / 1 GB VPS with no Node, no Redis and no reverse proxy, and tifa deploy puts it live.
hero.terminal: Terminal: creating and running a new app

stack.title: One file instead of a stack
stack.lead: No Node in production, no process manager, no reverse proxy, no Redis. The browser bundle, styles and server renderer are embedded in the executable.
rows: The Go HTTP server in the binary, which gets its own Let's Encrypt certificate and speaks HTTP/2
TanStack Router, rendered inside the Go process by [beastjs](https://github.com/liustack/beastjs), the fastest pure Go JavaScript engine for rendering React
An in-process render memo for pages, a CDN in front if you want one, plus whatever you keep in Go memory
SQLite, with [the fastest pure Go SQLite driver](https://github.com/liustack/sqlite), so CGO stays off

numbers.title: On one core
numbers.lead: Whole visits to the example shop, recorded from real browsers and played back against each server: shoppers, staff and crawlers at once.
numbers.caption: Each framework as shipped and warmed up with the same visits, one process on one core of a Google Cloud `t2d-standard-4` VM (AMD EPYC 7B13), 8 concurrent sessions with no think time, the median of 3 rounds, 2026-11-18. Tifa v0.1.0 with slowjs v0.31.6, Next.js 16.4.6, TanStack Start 1.169.3, Node 24.13.0. Not yet measured on a 1 CPU / 1 GB VPS.
cost: Tifa renders pages in beastjs, a pure Go JavaScript engine. It has no JIT, so one render takes longer than in Node.

With every request rendering, Next.js answers 1.17 times as many page requests as Tifa and TanStack Start 1.57 times, at 7 and 6 times Tifa's peak memory. See [the study](https://github.com/liustack/tifa/blob/v0.4.2/docs/studies/nextjs-and-tanstack-start.md#conclusions).

pages.title: Go loads, React renders
pages.lead: One folder per page. Go runs the page's `Load` first, then React renders complete HTML inside the process. The TypeScript type of the page's data is generated from what `Load` returns.
pages.legend: Fields Go returns, typed in React
notes: Real HTML on the first request
Search engines and link previews see the content, title and meta tags.
TanStack Router takes over in the browser. Each navigation is one request for data.
A `Load` result that cannot become TypeScript stops the build and names the file and line.

deploy.title: Push to deploy
deploy.lead: `tifa deploy setup` sets up the server, Cloudflare and GitHub Actions in one command. After that every push is checked and goes live, and a release that fails its health check rolls back by itself.

stages.text: To the default branch of your repository.
Runs `go tool tifa check` on the push.
When CI passes, builds the app for your server and runs `go tool tifa deploy`.
Through a Cloudflare Tunnel. The server opens no port: cloudflared on the server connects out to Cloudflare.

deploy.terminal: Terminal: a deploy from GitHub Actions
facts: Builds on your machine or in CI. Nothing is built on the server.
Restarts the app without refusing a request.
Checks `GET /healthz` once a second for up to 30 seconds, until it answers with a status below 500, and goes back to the release before when it does not.
The server needs no Docker, no Node and no deploy program of its own.
Several apps can share one server.

story.title: Why it exists
text: I wanted to ship a small product on TanStack Start. My other VPSes were full, Black Friday was still weeks away and I did not feel like buying another one, so I dug out an old box with 1 CPU and 1 GB of RAM. I had Codex set up the usual stack in one go: nginx, Node.js, PM2, TanStack Start, Redis, BullMQ, cron and SQLite.
It did not really run. It crawled.
So I started hacking on Tifa. Once it is done, deploying should mean copying one Go binary to the VPS, and that is it.

status.title: Status
rows: APIs will change, and many compiler optimizations are not done yet.
A framework like this touches the compiler, the bundler, server rendering and developer experience at once. Every line is written and reviewed by one author.
Bugs, ideas, confusing errors, unclear docs. A clear issue with steps to reproduce helps more than a patch. [Open an issue](https://github.com/liustack/tifa/issues/new/choose)
Under MIT your copy is yours to change and publish.

start.title: Start an app
start.req: You need Go 1.27 and Node 20.19 or 22.12 and later. Node only builds the front end: the program you deploy never needs it.
